local_facts.claim: Caltrans scheduled bridge-preservation work on eastbound I-10 in West Covina between Pacific Avenue/West Covina Parkway and Sunset Avenue, with recurring weekend ramp and lane closures continuing through fall 2026.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A freeway crash file should identify the travel direction, nearest ramp, lane, time, and any work-zone or detour condition. “I-10 in West Covina” is too broad to reconstruct the traffic setup or locate the right records.
local_facts.title: The I-10 scene may include ramp and work-zone conditions

local_facts.claim: West Covina’s 2022 Local Roadway Safety Plan, using 2017–2021 collision data, lists unsafe speed as the leading recorded cause at 24.4%, followed by improper turning at 19.5%; 34% of collisions occurred at night or during dusk or dawn.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Those are citywide patterns, not proof in one case. They show why the exact movement, signal or ramp, lighting, traffic conditions, and source of speed evidence should be documented rather than assumed.
local_facts.title: The location, lighting, and movement deserve to be recorded precisely

local_facts.claim: Los Angeles Superior Court lists West Covina as an East District court location and notes that Pomona civil cases were reassigned to the West Covina Courthouse on June 1, 2012. The Court also cautions that an address’s district does not necessarily determine where a case is or must be assigned.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A West Covina injury case should not be assumed to belong in the downtown courthouse merely because it is in Los Angeles County. Case type, local rules, and the facts govern the civil filing path.
local_facts.title: Los Angeles County civil filing has a local East District path

anchors.label: Court reporter per diem, Los Angeles Superior Court
anchors.detail: Three hundred eighty-two dollars for a civil proceeding running more than one hour but under four, and seven hundred sixty-four for four hours or more. Thirty dollars covers an hour or less.
anchors.source_name: Los Angeles Superior Court civil fee schedule

anchors.label: Complex case designation
anchors.detail: One thousand dollars for all plaintiffs and another thousand for each defendant, to a ceiling of $18,000 per case, on top of the ordinary first-paper fee.
anchors.source_name: Los Angeles Superior Court civil fee schedule

anchors.label: Daily jury deposit after the first day
anchors.detail: Los Angeles sets the running deposit at fifteen dollars per juror per day plus thirty-four cents a mile one way, deposited at the start of each session.
anchors.source_name: Los Angeles Superior Court civil fee schedule

anchors.label: Statutory percentage for an auto injury fee
anchors.detail: California controls the fee through an unconscionability standard and a written-contract statute. The rate itself is negotiated between the injured person and the lawyer.
anchors.source_name: Cal. Rules of Prof. Conduct, rule 1.5

fee_rows.note: First paper in an unlimited civil case, and again for each other party's first paper. Limited civil filings run $370 or $225 by pleaded amount.
fee_rows.source_name: Los Angeles Superior Court civil fee schedule

fee_rows.note: Sixty dollars for any paper requiring a hearing, including discovery motions and trial continuances; five hundred for summary judgment or summary adjudication.
fee_rows.source_name: Los Angeles Superior Court civil fee schedule

fee_rows.note: Nonrefundable, and waived if unpaid by the deadline. After day one the Los Angeles deposit is fifteen dollars per juror per day plus mileage.
Section 6147 requires the rate, the treatment of costs, and a statement that the fee is not set by law, in a contract signed by both sides.
